summary: Mobile SSO deep-link approvals leave temporary access in 'pending' despite console confirmation
description: Issue summary: Users approving access requests via the Okta mobile deep link (iOS/Android) sometimes see the console show the approval as successful, but the temporary role never materializes in RBAC and the access remains in a 'pending' state. Impact: Affected employees cannot perform just-in-time elevated actions (e.g., runbooks, support tools) even though the approval UI indicated success. This affects ~3-5% of mobile approvals in us-west during the window observed. Environment: Production (auth-service v2.14.1), Okta SSO, mobile deep-link flow, us-west region. Steps to reproduce: 1) From support portal, request temporary elevated role (JIT). 2) Approver opens Okta approval notification on mobile and taps the deep link. 3) Okta completes approval and redirects to redwood://auth/approval?token=... 4) Console shows approval success; approver receives success toast. 5) Requester remains in 'pending' with no RBAC grant. Observed behavior: Console shows success but backend audit events show the approval callback was received with 202 Accepted and returned before the RBAC engine applied the grant. In some cases the callback processing retried later and succeeded; in others it remained pending until manual retry. Initial logs show a race between the approval webhook handler and the role-propagation queue consumer. Expected behavior: Approval via mobile deep-link should result in the same synchronous or reliably-queued propagation path as web approvals, with RBAC grant applied within SLO (~30s). Investigation notes: - Spike in incidents correlates with auth-service deployment v2.14.1 (rolled 2026-03-09). - Mobile deep-link flow appends an auth callback parameter that hits /api/v1/approvals/callback which was refactored in v2.14.1 to return 202 early for mobile UX improvements. - The refactor moved role-propagation responsibility to an in-memory queue that can be GC'd if the approval handler instance scales down immediately after returning 202. - Reproducible in staging when artificially introducing pod scale-to-zero within 5s of callback. - Linked incident INT-472001 notes a similar approval callback race for SSO flows last year; potential overlap in the queueing logic. Temporary workaround: Avoid approving from the mobile deep link; instead approve from the web UI which uses the synchronous propagation path. Engineers can manually trigger a propagation retry via the console action "Reapply approvals" on the request. Next steps: 1) Revert the early-202 behavior in v2.14.1 for the approval callback OR persist queue messages to Redis (durable queue) before returning 202. 2) Add end-to-end e2e test that simulates pod scale-down during callback processing. 3) Add monitoring alert for approval callbacks that return 202 with no subsequent role-propagation audit events within 60s. 4) Patch and roll back with canary to us-west. Workaround rollout: Support agents notified to instruct approvers to use web UI until fix is live. Postmortem owner: Marta Nguyen.
